input: What are the major capital expenditure variances between authorized rate base filings and actual capital asset additions?
expected_output:
### Executive Summary
**Actual electric plant additions closed to Electric Plant in Service (FERC Account 101) exceeded authorized rate base determinations by $131.50M (+10.76%), primarily driven by transmission grid hardening and distribution substation modernizations. Transmission (FERC Accounts 350–359) and General/Intangible Plant (FERC Accounts 303, 389–399) exhibited the highest positive variances due to lead-time surcharges, supply chain inflation on high-voltage transformers, and enterprise grid management software capitalizations. Production plant additions experienced an unfavorable timing variance of -$17.70M (-9.83%) resulting from project inservice delays shifting target commercial operation dates into subsequent regulatory accounting periods.**

---

### Data Presentation: Plant Additions vs. Authorized Rate Base Filing

The reconciliation below analyzes capital expenditures placed in service (FERC Form 1, Pages 204–207, *Electric Plant in Service*, and Account 107 *Construction Work in Progress* transfers) compared against authorized baseline capital spending adopted in the most recent jurisdictional rate order.

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transmission Plant (Accounts 350–359)** | $489.20M | $412.50M | +18.59% | **Warning** |
| **Distribution Plant (Accounts 360–374)** | $598.40M | $545.00M | +9.80% | **Normal** |
| **Production / Generation Plant (Accounts 310–349)** | $162.30M | $180.00M | -9.83% | **Normal** |
| **General & Intangible Plant (Accounts 301–303, 389–399)** | $104.10M | $85.00M | +22.47% | **Critical** |
| **Total In-Service Plant Additions (Account 101)** | $1,354.00M | $1,222.50M | +10.76% | **Warning** |
| **AFUDC Equity/Debt Additions (Accounts 419.1 / 432)** | $42.60M | $36.10M | +18.01% | **Warning** |
| **CWIP Ending Balance (Account 107)** | $682.30M | $610.00M | +11.85% | **Normal** |
| **Plant Displacements / Retirements (Account 108/110)** | $74.20M | $78.00M | -4.87% | **Normal** |

---

### Key Variance Drivers & FERC Accounting Breakdown

1. **Transmission Additions (Accounts 352–356; +$76.70M / +18.59%)**:
   - **Interconnection & Capacity Upgrades**: High-voltage substation rebuilds and line reconductoring required to maintain NERC reliability standards under increased localized renewable injection.
   - **Cost Indexing**: Elevated EPC contract escalations and lead-time expediting fees for 230kV/500kV circuit breakers and power transformers.

2. **General & Intangible Plant (Accounts 303, 391, 397; +$19.10M / +22.47%)**:
   - **Cybersecurity & ADMS Capitalization**: Accelerated capital investment for NERC CIP compliance, Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS) modules, and fiber communications infrastructure.

3. **Production Plant (Accounts 310–346; -$17.70M / -9.83%)**:
   - **Turbine Retrofit Delay**: Gas turbine peaking plant overhaul slipped two quarters past target commercial operation date, delaying Account 107 transfer to Account 101 into the next fiscal year.

---

- **Prudence & Used/Useful Documentation**: Complete detailed Work Order Authorization (WOA) audit packets and cost-overrun justification memos for Transmission projects over budget by $>15\%$ to support used-and-useful showings in upcoming test-year rate base filings.
- **FERC Form 1 Footnote Disclosures**: Draft explanatory footnotes for FERC Form 1 Pages 204–207 and Page 216 (*Construction Work in Progress - Account 107*) detailing major transfers exceeding standard authorized thresholds.
- **AFUDC Accrual True-Up**: Audit Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) compound rates applied under Account 419.1/432 to prevent regulatory lag under-recoveries resulting from slipped production assets.
- **Regulatory Capital Tracker Alignment**: Coordinate with the Regulatory Strategy team to assess whether over-budget transmission capital additions qualify for rider/formula rate baseline updates or deferred asset accounting.
